pages.text: Taro grabbed a banana with muddy hands. "I'm hungry! Let's eat!" The hole he had just dug was still in the yard. "What about your hands?" Mumu asked, but Taro was already eating.
"Washing takes too long! My hands are fast." Taro peeled and gobbled the banana. Muddy handprints marked the bananas left behind.
Soon, Taro's tummy gurgled. He rubbed it and crouched on the porch. "Oh, my tummy..."
Sharp-eared deer Mumu heard and bounded over. Mumu held up a remaining banana. "Look. Muddy hand stamps." Taro's eyes widened.
"The mud on your hands rode the banana right into your tummy." Mumu took Taro to the yard basin, filled with well water.
Mumu dipped Taro's hands in. The soil loosened, turning the water yellowish. "Rub your palms! Wash the backs! Between each finger, one by one! Wash Hands First, Then Eat!"
Taro rinsed and shook his hands. When he picked up a fresh banana, not a muddy stamp appeared on the peel. He looked at his hands. "Wow! Everything I touched stayed clean!"
After a good rest, his sore tummy slowly improved, too. Taro tapped the porch with a branch and called, "Wash Hands First, Then Eat!"
Now Taro knew the washing steps. "One, dip hands in water! Two, clean between fingers one by one! Three, rinse and shake!" At snack time the next day, he ran to the basin before the bananas.

Mom, working on the porch, sat Taro on her lap and touched his hands. "They're lovely and clean." Washing first left no muddy stamps and kept his tummy comfortable. Taro waved his wet hands. "Mumu, wash yours, too! Wash Hands First, Then Eat!"
